Before she got the TB, Gramma Adie had gone to > to help out her eldest granddaughter—Claire’s “Se Joann. The divorce happened shortly after that when = found a Northern man who promised to take care “S Claire thought that was nice of the Northerner, but = had a lot of words for the man, even though he and & busted up pretty quick. Now, Gramma was back = Joann’s house and Joann still had plenty of trouble with 3 two kids to worry about a sickly old woman. =

Gramma had always had lung problems, but this was the first time she’d mentioned them in a \ letter. Joann and the boys are helping me out loads, . she wrote, I'd be dead already without them.

Grampa’s old typewriter sat in the hallway | between the house and the museum. She typed in near darkness, the only light shining in from Grampa’s workshop, where he was molding the limbs for Shiva. Grampa hadn’t used his typewriter since he’d stopped replying to Gramma’s letters. On account of his nearsightedness, she didn’t have to worry about Grampa seeing what she wrote.
